speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To understand what is happening inside you, can you tell me if you have been passing stool normally, and have you noticed any episodes of severe, colicky crying or drawing your legs up to your chest?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are fussy, eating less, and have a distended belly that hurts when touched. Given your age and these specific symptoms, I need to check for "currant jelly" stools (bloody mucus) and listen to your abdomen for high-pitched bowel sounds. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: The latest measurements show normal readings, but your symptoms of feeding difficulties and abdominal distension persist. To rule out other causes of obstruction or inflammation, can you confirm if there have been any episodes of vomiting, and do you recall if you were born prematurely or had any recent infections? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound results are normal, which makes intussusception and mechanical obstruction less likely. Given your persistent feeding difficulties, vomiting, and distension, do you have any history of Hirschsprung disease, and are you currently passing green, bilious stool? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray reveals dilated bowel segments and an empty rectum, confirming a high intestinal obstruction. Given your age and the absence of a transition zone on the X-ray, could you confirm if you have a history of chronic constipation or meconium ileus? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal CT with contrast.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT scan results showing normal readings are confusing given the previous X-ray suggested obstruction; this discrepancy requires immediate clarification. Can you tell me if the vomiting is bilious (green) or if there has been any history of failure to pass meconium within the first 24 hours of life? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray (Repeat).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction

speaker: Doctor
text: The repeat X-ray is normal, which contradicts the earlier finding of obstruction; this inconsistency is concerning. Has the baby passed any meconium within the first 24 hours of life, and was there a history of severe constipation as an infant? REQUEST TEST: Contrast Enema.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: A transition zone in the distal colon, compatible with Hirschsprung disease
